input.prompt:
Build a homepage design preview for Marcus Webb's personal portfolio.

PROJECT DETAILS:
- Name: Marcus Webb
- Profession: Freelance graphic designer
- Aesthetic: Minimal & sophisticated

DESIGN DIRECTION:
Editorial minimalism — generous whitespace, confident typography hierarchy, and restrained color. The page should feel like a well-designed print piece brought to life. Sophisticated without being cold; minimal without being empty.

LAYOUT TYPE: Standard
Marketing/portfolio site with full navigation structure.

VISUAL DIRECTION:
- Color: Near-black (#0F0F0F) base with warm off-white (#F7F5F2) backgrounds. ONE subtle accent — a muted warm gold or deep terracotta used sparingly on hover states and dividers. No bright colors.
- Typography: Serif display font (Playfair Display or DM Serif Display) for the hero name and section headings — elegant and editorial. Clean sans-serif (DM Sans or Outfit) for body and nav. Dramatic size contrast between headings and body.
- Layout: Asymmetric hero with oversized name as the dominant visual element. Thin horizontal rules as section dividers. Generous vertical rhythm.
- Visual elements: No photography needed. Typography IS the visual. Subtle geometric line accents (thin rules, small squares) as decorative elements.
- Motion: Subtle — staggered fade-up entrance on hero text (400ms, ease-out), gentle underline-draw hover on nav links, soft fade-in on scroll for sections. Nothing bouncy.

LOGO:
Use the media-logo skill to generate a wordmark-style logo for "MW" — minimal monogram mark, clean and geometric.

MOTION DESIGN:
- Level: Subtle
- Effects: Hero text staggered fade-up (name first, then tagline, then CTA — 150ms stagger), fade-in on scroll for About and Contact sections (350ms ease-out), underline-draw on nav hover (200ms), subtle opacity shift on social icon hover
- Personality: Quiet and deliberate — motion should feel like turning a page, not a tech demo

SECTION-SPECIFIC:

Hero:
- Full-viewport height
- Oversized "Marcus Webb" in serif display font — large enough to feel architectural (clamp to ~10-14vw)
- Tagline below: "Freelance Graphic Designer — crafting visual identities that endure"
- Thin horizontal rule above and below the name
- Subtle "Scroll" indicator at bottom with a small animated arrow
- Staggered fade-up entrance animation

About:
- Two-column layout: left has a large section number ("01") in muted tone, right has the content
- Headline: "About"
- Body: 2-3 paragraphs — Marcus is a freelance graphic designer with 8+ years of experience crafting brand identities, print collateral, and visual systems for clients across fashion, hospitality, and culture. He believes great design is invisible — it communicates before words do. Based in Los Angeles, available worldwide.
- Skills listed as a clean horizontal row of tags (Brand Identity · Typography · Print · Art Direction · Visual Systems)
- Fade-in on scroll

Contact:
- Clean, minimal layout
- Section number "02" treatment matching About
- Headline: "Let's Work Together"
- Short line: "Open to new projects and collaborations."
- Email as a large, styled link: hello@marcuswebb.co — with underline-draw hover
- Social icons row: Behance, Instagram, LinkedIn — minimal icon style, subtle hover opacity
- NO colored CTA band — just elegant typography and spacing

Footer:
- Single line: "© 2024 Marcus Webb — All rights reserved"
- Matches the minimal, editorial tone

DIFFERENTIATION:
The oversized hero name that functions as both headline and visual artwork — it should feel like a poster, not a website header.

CONSISTENCY:
Maintain editorial restraint throughout. The contact section should feel as considered as the hero. No section should feel like an afterthought.

BUILD ORDER:

Phase 1 — Setup (run in parallel):
- Set font stack using fontTheme tool: DM Serif Display (display/headings) + DM Sans (body/UI)
- Set color scheme using colorScheme tool: near-black foreground (#0F0F0F), warm off-white background (#F7F5F2), muted warm gold accent
- Generate logo using media-logo skill: "MW" monogram, minimal geometric style

Phase 2 — Structure (run in parallel, after Phase 1):
- Build Header: minimal nav — "Marcus Webb" wordmark left, nav links right (Work, About, Contact). Underline-draw hover. Transparent over hero, solid on scroll.
- Build Footer: single-line minimal footer

Phase 3 — Page (after Phase 1 & 2):
- Build homepage (index.tsx) with hero, about, and contact sections with all animations

Phase 4 — Finalize:
- Mark "Homepage" todo item as complete using todoList tool
- Ask for design feedback using askQuestion

INITIAL SCOPE:
Build ONLY the homepage for this preview.

DESIGN FEEDBACK:
After showing the design, use askQuestion to ask:
- Question: "What do you think of the design, Marcus?"
- Suggestions: ["Love it — let's build the portfolio gallery", "Change the color scheme", "Adjust the typography", "Tweak the layout or spacing"]

Let's go. I'll build both — case studies first, then the contact form. Starting with the case study page now.Good — I have the full project data. Now I'll build the case study page, contact page, and update routes all in parallel.Now update routes and the work gallery to use the shared projects data:Now update the work gallery to pull from the shared data file, and update the homepage contact section to link to `/contact`:Now update the homepage contact section to link to `/contact` page:Also add Contact to the header nav:Now mark both todos complete:The site is now fully built. **Case study pages** (`/work/[id]`) — each project gets a full editorial layout with a large hero image, Overview / Challenge / Approach / Outcome narrative, a sidebar with services and deliverables, and prev/next navigation to move between projects. All six projects have unique, detailed copy.

**Contact page** (`/contact`) — a two-column layout with your contact details on the left and a clean inquiry form on the right. The form includes name, email, company, project type chips, budget range chips, and a message field. On submit it shows a confirmation state. No colored CTA bands — just typography and spacing, consistent with the rest of the site.

**Navigation** is now fully wired — Work, About, and Contact all live in the header with active-state underlines, and the homepage contact section links through to the full inquiry form.

export interface Project {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  client: string;
  year: string;
  category: string;
  slot: string;
  tagline: string;
  overview: string;
  challenge: string;
  solution: string;
  outcome: string;
  services: string[];
  deliverables: string[];
  color: string; // subtle bg tint for hero
}

export const projects: Project[] = [
  {
    id: 'maison-arc',
    title: 'Maison Arc',
    client: 'Maison Arc',
    year: '2024',
    category: 'Brand Identity',
    slot: '/airo-assets/images/portfolio/brand-identity-1',
    tagline: 'A refined identity for a Parisian-inspired interiors studio.',
    overview:
      'Maison Arc is a Los Angeles–based interiors studio drawing on French modernist principles. They needed a brand identity that felt both rooted in heritage and unmistakably contemporary.',
    challenge:
      'The existing brand lacked cohesion — a mismatched logotype, inconsistent color usage, and no clear typographic system. The studio was growing rapidly and needed a visual language that could scale across print, digital, and environmental applications.',
    solution:
      'We developed a wordmark built around a custom-drawn letterform for the "A" — an architectural arch that echoes the studio\'s name and design philosophy. The palette draws from raw plaster, aged brass, and deep shadow. A strict typographic system pairs a refined serif display with a geometric sans for body copy.',
    outcome:
      'The new identity launched across a full suite of stationery, signage, and a redesigned website. Client inquiries increased by 40% in the first quarter following launch, and the studio was featured in Architectural Digest\'s emerging studios roundup.',
    services: ['Brand Strategy', 'Identity Design', 'Typography', 'Art Direction'],
    deliverables: ['Logo System', 'Brand Guidelines', 'Stationery Suite', 'Signage Templates', 'Digital Assets'],
    color: '#F5F0EB',
  },
  {
    id: 'forma-editorial',
    title: 'Forma Editorial',
    client: 'Forma Magazine',
    year: '2024',
    category: 'Typography',
    slot: '/airo-assets/images/portfolio/typography-2',
    tagline: 'A typographic identity for an independent design publication.',
    overview:
      'Forma is an independent quarterly magazine covering contemporary design, architecture, and material culture. The publication needed a typographic identity as considered as its editorial content.',
    challenge:
      'Independent magazines live and die by their visual distinctiveness on the newsstand. Forma needed a masthead and typographic system that felt authoritative and collectible — something readers would recognize immediately and keep on their shelves.',
    solution:
      'The masthead uses a custom-modified condensed serif, letterfit by hand for optical precision. A strict grid system governs every spread, with a secondary typeface chosen for its contrast in weight and texture. Drop caps, pull quotes, and folios each have their own typographic rules, creating a consistent rhythm across every issue.',
    outcome:
      'Forma\'s redesign sold out its first print run of 2,000 copies within three weeks. The publication was shortlisted for the Stack Awards\' Best New Magazine category and has since grown to a subscriber base of over 8,000.',
    services: ['Typographic Design', 'Editorial Design', 'Grid Systems', 'Art Direction'],
    deliverables: ['Masthead Design', 'Type System', 'Grid Templates', 'Style Guide', 'Cover Templates'],
    color: '#F2F2F0',
  },
  {
    id: 'sable-skincare',
    title: 'Sable Skincare',
    client: 'Sable',
    year: '2023',
    category: 'Packaging',
    slot: '/airo-assets/images/portfolio/packaging-3',
    tagline: 'Minimal packaging for a luxury skincare line rooted in ritual.',
    overview:
      'Sable is a direct-to-consumer skincare brand built around slow beauty rituals and sustainably sourced ingredients. Their packaging needed to communicate luxury without excess.',
    challenge:
      'The skincare market is saturated with brands competing on shelf presence through color and pattern. Sable wanted to stand apart through restraint — packaging that felt like an object worth keeping, not discarding.',
    solution:
      'We stripped the packaging back to its essentials: uncoated stock, blind embossing, and a single ink color per product line. The logotype is set in a custom-spaced small caps, and product names are typeset with deliberate negative space. Every element earns its place.',
    outcome:
      'Sable\'s packaging won a Dieline Award in the Beauty & Personal Care category. The brand was picked up by Goop and Net-a-Porter within six months of launch, and the packaging has been featured in over 40 design publications.',
    services: ['Packaging Design', 'Brand Identity', 'Typography', 'Production Oversight'],
    deliverables: ['Primary Packaging', 'Secondary Packaging', 'Label System', 'Unboxing Experience', 'Brand Standards'],
    color: '#F7F4F0',
  },
  {
    id: 'grove-annual',
    title: 'Grove Annual Report',
    client: 'Grove Collective',
    year: '2023',
    category: 'Print',
    slot: '/airo-assets/images/portfolio/print-4',
    tagline: 'An annual report that reads like a manifesto.',
    overview:
      'Grove Collective is a nonprofit focused on urban reforestation and community green space. Their annual report needed to reflect the weight of their mission while remaining accessible and compelling to donors.',
    challenge:
      'Most nonprofit annual reports are functional but forgettable — dense with data, light on design. Grove wanted something their donors would actually read, and that would make the case for continued investment through visual storytelling.',
    solution:
      'We structured the report as a narrative journey, opening with a full-bleed photographic essay before transitioning into data visualization and impact metrics. A warm, earthy palette and generous white space give the data room to breathe. Custom infographics translate complex environmental data into clear, elegant visuals.',
    outcome:
      'Donor retention increased by 22% in the year following the report\'s release. Grove received three unsolicited major gifts from new donors who cited the report as their introduction to the organization. The report was recognized by the AIGA as a Communication Design Excellence honoree.',
    services: ['Print Design', 'Data Visualization', 'Editorial Design', 'Production Management'],
    deliverables: ['64-Page Annual Report', 'Digital PDF Version', 'Infographic System', 'Print-Ready Files'],
    color: '#F0F4EE',
  },
  {
    id: 'lune-campaign',
    title: 'Lune Campaign',
    client: 'Lune Studio',
    year: '2023',
    category: 'Art Direction',
    slot: '/airo-assets/images/portfolio/art-direction-5',
    tagline: 'Art direction for a fragrance campaign rooted in memory.',
    overview:
      'Lune Studio is an independent fragrance house creating scents inspired by specific moments in time. Their debut campaign needed to translate the intangible — memory, atmosphere, sensation — into a visual language.',
    challenge:
      'Fragrance is notoriously difficult to communicate visually. The campaign needed to evoke emotional resonance without relying on cliché imagery, and had to work across print, OOH, and digital formats simultaneously.',
    solution:
      'We built the campaign around the concept of "the moment before" — images that capture anticipation rather than action. Soft, directional light. Figures in partial silhouette. Negative space used as a compositional element. The copy was stripped to single words, letting the imagery carry the weight.',
    outcome:
      'The campaign ran across print, Instagram, and a limited OOH placement in New York and Los Angeles. Lune\'s debut collection sold out in 11 days. The campaign imagery was licensed for use in a feature on independent fragrance in Vogue.',
    services: ['Art Direction', 'Creative Strategy', 'Campaign Design', 'Photography Direction'],
    deliverables: ['Campaign Concept', 'Print Ads', 'Social Assets', 'OOH Formats', 'Campaign Guidelines'],
    color: '#F3F0F5',
  },
  {
    id: 'atlas-identity',
    title: 'Atlas Visual System',
    client: 'Atlas Agency',
    year: '2022',
    category: 'Brand Identity',
    slot: '/airo-assets/images/portfolio/visual-system-6',
    tagline: 'A scalable visual system for a global creative agency.',
    overview:
      'Atlas is a full-service creative agency with offices in Los Angeles, London, and Tokyo. After a period of rapid growth, their brand had fragmented across regions. They needed a unified visual system that could flex across cultures while remaining unmistakably Atlas.',
    challenge:
      'With three offices operating semi-independently, Atlas had accumulated three slightly different logos, two color palettes, and no consistent typographic approach. The rebrand needed to unify without erasing the regional character each office had developed.',
    solution:
      'We developed a modular identity system built around a single geometric mark — an "A" constructed from intersecting lines that can be read as a compass, a map pin, or an architectural form depending on context. The system includes a primary palette with three regional accent colors, a two-typeface system, and a comprehensive set of layout templates.',
    outcome:
      'The new identity system was rolled out across all three offices simultaneously. Atlas reported a 35% reduction in time spent on brand approvals in the first year, and the agency won three new business pitches in which the rebrand was cited as a differentiating factor.',
    services: ['Brand Strategy', 'Identity Design', 'Design Systems', 'Brand Governance'],
    deliverables: ['Logo System', 'Brand Guidelines (180pp)', 'Template Library', 'Motion Guidelines', 'Brand Portal'],
    color: '#EEF0F4',
  },
];

export function getProject(id: string): Project | undefined {
  return projects.find((p) => p.id === id);
}

export function getAdjacentProjects(id: string): { prev: Project | null; next: Project | null } {
  const idx = projects.findIndex((p) => p.id === id);
  return {
    prev: idx > 0 ? projects[idx - 1] : null,
    next: idx < projects.length - 1 ? projects[idx + 1] : null,
  };
}
